s09.client_chat.cc_001: Ariane Bosch, special risks, Havenkring. I'll be quick because I have a claim clock running and it is not on my side.
s09.client_chat.cc_002: Twelfth of March, 03:40, Vrijthof fair, hall B. Three men, a service door, a cutting disc and a very small charge. Case Four only. In and out in four minutes.
s09.client_chat.cc_003: Gone: a Thracian gold diadem on loan from Plovdiv, insured with us at five point four, and the two gold appliqués that stood either side of it. Six other insured objects in the same case were not touched. One man was arrested in the loading bay. Twenty-two, local. He has not opened his mouth since.
s09.client_chat.cc_004: Here is my problem and it is not a moral one. The police have a burglary. Burglaries get paid. I have fourteen days to find a reason not to pay and after that the claim is admitted by default.
s09.client_chat.cc_005: So I am not asking you who they are. The police can have them. I am asking whether this was arranged from inside the stand, because if it was, the policy is paper and I keep six million euro.
s09.client_chat.cc_006: The gallery's registrar has volunteered her phone. Twenty-six years old, she installed that case with her own hands, and she rang me — I did not ring her. Make of that what you like, I have.
s09.client_chat.cc_007: It is live and it is on the desk in front of me and she is sitting in reception with a coffee. Are you taking it?
s09.client_chat.cc_008: Good. Start with what her job actually is, because the whole thing is going to turn on paperwork, it always does.
s09.client_chat.cc_009: One warning. Everybody in this trade is charming and everybody has known everybody for thirty years. Do not let that do any work in your head.
s09.interstitial.is1_001: Four minutes and they went to one case.
s09.interstitial.is1_002: There are ninety-one stands in that hall. Eleven of them have gold in the window. They walked past all of it in the dark. They stopped at Case Four. It is not the biggest case. It is not the most valuable case, and it is forty metres from the door they came in by.
s09.interstitial.is1_003: Nobody walks forty metres in a building they do not know. Keep going.
s09.interstitial.is2_002: The schedule I am insuring says nine objects. Her installation photograph shows ten. And she took that photograph at 16:20 on the fourth of March with the courier standing next to her, because that is the procedure and she followed it.
s09.interstitial.is2_003: I have been doing this for nineteen years and I have never once had the number be wrong in that direction. Short, yes. Never long.
s09.interstitial.is2_004: Find me the tenth thing. Nobody has reported a tenth thing.
s09.interstitial.is3_001: Right. I have read Haddad's list twice and had a very long lunch with our reinsurers' counsel, who has stopped enjoying this case.
s09.interstitial.is3_002: Thirty-one objects out of one hole in the ground, sold through one stand over thirteen years, and the only thing that ties them to each other is a piece of ivory the size of a postcard with a shopping list scratched on it.
s09.interstitial.is3_003: Which is why it was in that case. He could not leave it in a safe. He could not put it in a catalogue. So he kept it where he could see it. Then he had somebody take the whole case, so the one thing he actually needed to lose went out with the gold.
s09.interstitial.is3_004: Finish it. I want the arrangement, not the theory.
s09.closing_chat.cl_001: Guus Halderman. I have had to say it out loud a few times to get used to it.
s09.closing_chat.cl_002: The alarm zone for Case Four was isolated for installation on the second of March. It was re-armed on the fourth. Then it was suppressed again at 22:14 on the eleventh, from the stand's own tablet. That tablet is signed into one account.
s09.closing_chat.cl_003: The vitrine was refitted eleven days before opening, out of cycle, on his order, with a lock the fitter says he was asked for by name.
s09.closing_chat.cl_004: And nine thousand euro left the gallery in three payments to a twenty-two-year-old ex-porter, described as photography.
s09.closing_chat.cl_005: So. Policy repudiated, six million stays in Rotterdam, and I have a very good quarter.
s09.closing_chat.cl_006: Except that is not the whole file and we both know it.
s09.closing_chat.cl_007: If I go with the arrangement alone, the plaque never surfaces. It cannot. The only person who can prove it was in that case is Lotte Vervoort. She signed a condition report that says nine, because Halderman stood over her and told her nine. She was twenty-five, eight months into her first job.
s09.closing_chat.cl_008: If I put the whole thing in — the plaque, the inscription, Haddad's list — then everything changes. Thirty-one acquisitions across six countries come apart. A site nobody has been able to name gets named, and my claim question disappears into a criminal investigation that will run for four years. I will almost certainly have to pay.
s09.closing_chat.cl_009: And there is a third road, which is Lotte's, and which she asked me about this morning and I have not answered.
s09.closing_chat.cl_010: She goes to the heritage inspectorate herself, first, before I file anything. She has a false condition report with her signature on it and no immunity yet. Slower, riskier, and Halderman gets a week's warning to burn whatever is left. But it is her name on that report and she would like to be the one who says so.
s09.closing_chat.cl_011: Fourteen days is now two. Tell me which file I write.
s09.closing_chat.cl_011.opt1: The arrangement only. Void the policy, keep the money.
s09.closing_chat.cl_011.opt2: All of it. The plaque, the list, the site.
s09.closing_chat.cl_013: Repudiation it is. Clean, provable, and finished inside the month.
s09.closing_chat.cl_014: I want it noted between us: this is the right answer to the question I was actually paid to ask, and I know exactly which question I am not asking.
s09.closing_chat.cl_015: All of it, then. I will hand the reinsurers a four-year hole in the ground and a bill, and I will do it on Thursday.
s09.closing_chat.cl_016: Nineteen years I have been finding reasons not to pay. This will be the first time I have found one and handed it in anyway.
s09.closing_chat.cl_017: Hers, then. She goes first and I sit on my hands for a week, which at my time of life is a genuinely novel experience.
s09.closing_chat.cl_018: If he burns it, he burns it. She is the only person in this entire file who has done one single thing she did not have to, and I am not going to be the one who takes that off her to save a fortnight.
s09.closing_chat.cl_019: Good work. Send me the invoice today, not next week — after Thursday I may not have a budget line.
s09.ending.policy:
The policy was repudiated on 4 May on the ground that the loss was occasioned by an act of the insured. Havenkring paid nothing. Plovdiv's museum had insured nothing itself, because the borrower's cover was a condition of the loan. It received nothing either. Its diadem has not been seen since.

Guus Halderman was charged with fraud and with organising the burglary. He pleaded to the fraud, received twenty-two months of which he served nine, and the gallery was wound up in the spring. The trade absorbed it the way the trade absorbs everything: at the following year's fair, two of his former colleagues were overheard describing it as a sad business and a great loss to scholarship.

The ivory plaque was never mentioned in any charge, because the only evidence that it was ever in Case Four was one photograph on the phone of a registrar who had signed a document saying there were nine objects in it.

Rima Haddad's list still runs to thirty-one entries. She emailed Ariane Bosch twice in the following year and received a short, polite, entirely truthful reply both times.

Lotte Vervoort was not prosecuted. She was also not employable, and she now works for a firm that photographs kitchens for estate agents. She is very good at it.
s09.ending.everything:
The file went to the heritage inspectorate, the public prosecutor and — on the same afternoon, on Ariane Bosch's own initiative — to Dr Rima Haddad in Berlin.

The claim question was never determined. It was absorbed into a criminal investigation that ran four years and eight months, and Havenkring paid the €6 million in the second year on counsel's advice, plus costs. Bosch was moved sideways within eleven months and left the industry in the third year.

What the plaque did: its inscription is a burial inventory, and it names, in order, the objects laid in one chamber at Tell Muqbila. Twenty-nine of the thirty-one on Haddad's list are now matched to it by name. Six museums in four countries have deaccessioned. Two are litigating. One has published a full acquisition history of its Near Eastern holdings, going back to 1968. Nobody asked it to do that. It has been quietly devastating for everybody else.

Guus Halderman was convicted of fraud, handling and dealing in unlawfully removed cultural property. Four years.

Lotte Vervoort gave evidence for nine days. She is now the collections manager of a mid-sized municipal museum in the east of the country, where she has instituted an installation procedure that several colleagues have described, without affection, as excessive.
s09.ending.lotte:
Lotte Vervoort walked into the heritage inspectorate on the Monday morning with her own photographs, her own condition report, and a solicitor she had paid for herself.

She got seven days of nothing happening, which was the risk. Halderman used four of them. The gallery's pre-2014 acquisition files do not exist any more and the hard drive that held the stand's tablet backups was replaced by an IT contractor who has produced an invoice for it.

What survived is what was already on her phone, which is why the case ran at all. She was granted immunity on the false report on the second day and has never been charged with anything.

Halderman was convicted on the plaque, and on nineteen of the thirty-one. Not all thirty-one — twelve of the provenance files went missing in the four days after. Three years and six months. Havenkring repudiated the policy on the arrangement evidence and did not pay, which Ariane Bosch has described in writing as a result she is not going to pretend she is unhappy about.

Tell Muqbila was named in a UNESCO annexe the following autumn. Rima Haddad's list is down to twelve.

Bosch's last message was sent from an airport and reads in full: she went in on her own with a solicitor she could not afford, which in this trade is the single most eccentric thing I have ever heard of, and I have been doing it since 2007.

s09.mail.gm_005.subject: Re: your enquiry — Tell Muqbila documentation project
s09.mail.gm_005.body:
Dear Ms Vervoort,

Thank you for writing and please do not apologise for the hour, I answer these at strange hours myself.

Yes. The object you describe matches item 1 on our list: ivory, incised, roughly 11 by 7 centimetres, with an incised list in five ruled registers. We have never located it. We have always assumed it was destroyed.

I should explain why it matters more than the rest. It is not valuable. It is a burial inventory: it names, in order, what was laid in the chamber. If it exists, then thirty-one objects that have appeared on the market since 2011 stop being unprovenanced and start being a list, and a list has a place attached to it.

I have attached the concordance. Please look at entries 4, 9, 17 and 26 and tell me whether you have handled any of them.

I understand this may be difficult for you professionally. I have been doing this for seven years and you are the first person from inside the trade who has written to me first.

With thanks,
Dr Rima Haddad

s09.messages.f_sms_101: Ms Vervoort — exhibitor pack for Vrijthof 2026 is in your inbox. Please return the signed stand agreement, the staff list for badges and the nominated key holder by 31 January. J. Prins, Fair Registrar.

s09.messages.f_sms_128: I keep a copy for seven years. Everybody in this trade does. You want one, you ask me and I will send it, I have got nothing to hide and neither have you.

s09.messages.f_sms_148: Thank you for today. You are the first registrar in eleven years who counted with me instead of handing me a form. I have written that to my director.

s09.chats.f_wa_135: they have taken my roster off me and given it to the lawyers. I put it in writing twice and I am glad I did
s09.chats.f_wa_136: I am off hall B now. moved to the car parks. that is how it works here

s09.chats.f_wa_153: You signed a document you knew was wrong and you photographed the thing that made it wrong. One of those is a problem for you. The other one is the reason I am talking to you and not about you.

s09.messages.f2_sms_201: Ms Vervoort — I am asked to pass on that exhibitor property in hall B will be released in tranches and that a schedule will follow. I have been asking for that schedule since the twentieth of March.
s09.messages.f2_sms_202: Thank you. Is there a form I should be filling in that I do not know about? I would rather be early with it than chase it.
s09.messages.f2_sms_203: There is no form. That is the difficulty. There is no form because nobody has ever had to do this here before.
s09.messages.f2_sms_204: Between us: I have put in my notice. Twenty-two years. I am not going to make a speech about it in a text message.
s09.messages.f2_sms_205: I am sorry to hear that. Genuinely.
s09.messages.f2_sms_206: Don't be. I would rather leave than sit through a season of pretending the halls were always run properly. You will understand that better than most people I could say it to.
s09.messages.f2_sms_211: Rob — you said you keep copies of your work orders for seven years. Could I have the ones for B14. All of them, including the low cases.
s09.messages.f2_sms_212: Sent. Three of them. Two are the fair's own jobs and one is yours.
s09.messages.f2_sms_213: Thank you. Do you want to know why I am asking?
s09.messages.f2_sms_214: No. I want to be able to say nobody told me anything. You keep your records, I keep mine, and that is how this trade is supposed to work.
s09.messages.f2_sms_221: A month, as I said. Nothing to answer. The peonies are out here and that is the whole of my news.
s09.messages.f2_sms_222: Lotte. I am writing at a normal hour for once. I have been asked by our lawyer to stop writing to you and I have told her that I write to colleagues and that I will continue.
s09.messages.f2_sms_223: Dr Ilieva, I have not answered. I do not know how to write to you without lying, or saying something I am not allowed to say yet. Those have been the only two options for three weeks.
s09.messages.f2_sms_224: Then there is a third. Write to me about nothing. I will accept nothing from you very happily.
s09.messages.f2_sms_225: The humidity in my flat is 61 and I have bought a meter.
s09.messages.f2_sms_226: Now that is a proper letter. 61 is too high. Buy a plant.
s09.chats.f2_wa_201: The hall is not releasing anything. I have told the insurers we are entirely in their hands, which is true and does us no harm.
s09.chats.f2_wa_202: The loan crates are still in there. Dr Ilieva's museum will want a written position and I do not have one to give them.
s09.chats.f2_wa_203: Then do not give them one yet. Nobody is served by us putting things in writing this week.
s09.chats.f2_wa_204: I gave my statement to Havenkring this morning. Straightforward. They asked about the install and I said you had run it beautifully, which is what I have said to everybody.
s09.chats.f2_wa_206: Lotte, ring me. Not about any of this. I would just rather hear your voice than look at a screen with your name on it.
s09.chats.f2_wa_207: I have been told you were in Rotterdam for six hours. Six hours is not a witness, six hours is a project. I am not angry. I would like to be told things by you rather than about you.
s09.chats.f2_wa_208: Whatever you think you have understood, I would ask you to consider that you have been in this trade for eight months and I have been in it for thirty-two years, and that the difference between those two numbers is mostly things that look worse than they are.
s09.chats.f2_wa_221: Technical came back on the contact sheet. Bar in every frame, consistent, timestamped, no gaps in the sequence. They used the word exemplary, which I have never heard them use about an exhibitor.
s09.chats.f2_wa_222: That is just how it is done.
s09.chats.f2_wa_223: It is how it is supposed to be done. It is not how it is done. Learn the difference, it is going to matter to you.
s09.chats.f2_wa_224: It is twenty past three and I have written him an email I am not going to send. Is that something I should tell you about.
s09.chats.f2_wa_225: Do not send it. Keep it. And yes — tell me about anything you write to him, before you write it if you can manage it.
s09.chats.f2_wa_226: Am I allowed to still like him.
s09.chats.f2_wa_227: Yes. Everybody who has ever been taken in by somebody liked them, that is the mechanism. It has no bearing on what you do next.
s09.chats.f2_wa_228: The museum have written to me about you unprompted. Two paragraphs, and not one of them was about the objects. I am telling you because you will not have been told.
s09.chats.f2_wa_241: car parks for six weeks now. I have applied for three other jobs and told all three of them why

s09.mail.f2_gm_201.subject: ATA carnet 26/NL/4471 — second notice
s09.mail.f2_gm_201.body:
The carnet remains undischarged. Re-importation vouchers have not been presented.

Where goods cannot be re-imported within the validity, the holder must apply for regularisation and provide evidence of the circumstances. A police reference number is acceptable evidence. A letter from the holder is not.
s09.mail.f2_gm_202.subject: ATA carnet 26/NL/4471 — final notice
s09.mail.f2_gm_202.body:
This is a final notice before the guarantee is called.

We understand from your correspondence that the goods are held by the police and that you are unable to obtain a release. We are obliged to tell you that this does not suspend the validity of the carnet, and that the guaranteeing association will be approached on 1 June.
s09.mail.f2_gm_203.subject: Return leg — crew turned away (2nd attempt)
s09.mail.f2_gm_203.body:
Our crew attended the hall B loading bay this morning and were turned away for the second time. We are not going to send them a third time.

Tell us when there is something to collect and we will come within 48 hours. Until then the booking is cancelled and there is nothing owing.
s09.mail.f2_gm_204.subject: Your account
s09.mail.f2_gm_204.body:

This is the fourth fair we have done with your gallery and you are the only person there who has ever answered an email from us on the same day. That is not nothing.
s09.mail.f2_gm_205.subject: Crate hire — the four units
s09.mail.f2_gm_205.body:
Still suspended, still not accruing. You have now asked us three times whether this is a problem for us and it is still not a problem for us.

When you get them back, check the lids against the numbers you wrote on the hire note. You are the only customer who has ever done that and I would hate for the one time it mattered to be this one.
s09.mail.f2_gm_206.subject: Inbeslaggenomen goederen — procedure
s09.mail.f2_gm_206.body:
Property seized in connection with an investigation is released on the authority of the public prosecutor and not by this office.

An application for release may be made by the owner or by a person with a demonstrable right. Where ownership is itself in question, the application will not be considered until that question is resolved.

No estimate of timescale can be given.

s09.mail.f2_gm_207.body:

s09.mail.f2_gm_208.subject: Claim HK-26-0331 — position

s09.mail.f2_gm_212.body:
Dear Ms Vervoort,

s09.mail.f2_gm_213.subject: Re: Reference
s09.mail.f2_gm_213.body:
Lotte,

Of course. Send them my details and I will write it tonight.

You did not need the two paragraphs of explanation. I deleted them without reading past the first line. I know that is a slightly theatrical thing to do. You taught the second years for me and you were the only postgraduate who ever made them write the number down before anybody said the number.

Ring me when it is over. Not before.

Anneke
